steps: The current state records where the robot is, its velocity, and the safe time interval.
Candidate acceleration primitives determine reachable next velocities, travel durations, and arrival times.
A transition is accepted only if its motion fits the speed and acceleration limits and avoids blocked intervals; a wait requires zero speed.

kinodynamic_sipp.best_for: Use it when schedules must respect velocity and acceleration, not only when a graph vertex is occupied.
kinodynamic_sipp.watch_out: Integer ticks, finite motion limits, and the supplied primitive model define the reachable states. Waiting while moving is not allowed by this contract.
kinodynamic_sipp.evaluation: Validate both temporal collision freedom and every velocity/acceleration transition. Compare arrival, waiting, and dynamic feasibility using identical tick size and limits; spatial path length alone is insufficient.

eecbs.tagline: Resolve one collision, then send the agents again.
eecbs.story: Two individually good routes may ask different agents to occupy the same cell at the same time. EECBS searches over conflict constraints, asking the low-level planners to find new routes around each discovered collision.
steps: Plan a route for each agent on the shared graph.
Detect a vertex conflict or an edge-swap conflict.
Branch on constraints that forbid the collision and replan the affected agent.
eecbs.experiment: Watch the paths cross. The meeting is not a goal; it is a conflict that creates a new planning choice.
eecbs.question: Which movement conflicts are in this project's EECBS contract?
eecbs.answer: Vertex conflicts and edge swaps on an undirected unit-weight graph, with unique starts and goals.
eecbs.mechanism: EECBS is a two-level multi-agent search. At the high level it maintains candidate joint plans and resolves detected conflicts with constraints; at the low level it replans an individual agent under those constraints. Explicit Estimation Search helps order high-level conflict-tree nodes, while focal search guides low-level paths. The configured weight is part of the bounded-suboptimal contract.

example.setup: Two agents plan through a narrow corridor and choose the same vertex at the same timestep.
steps: The low level finds an individual route for each agent under the current constraints.
The high level detects a vertex conflict or an edge swap and branches by forbidding one agent's conflicting action in each child.
Only the affected agent is replanned in each child; search continues until a conflict-free joint plan is found or the run stops.

eecbs.best_for: Use it for undirected unit-weight MAPF graphs with unique starts and goals, vertex and edge-swap conflicts, and the stay-at-goal convention.
eecbs.watch_out: The project's w>=1 bound is meaningful only for a successful result under the supported conflict and cost model. Different MAPF objectives or conflict rules are different problems.
eecbs.evaluation: Report conflict-free success, sum of costs and makespan separately, runtime, and high-level expansions. Compare with identical maps, agent sets, conflict rules, stay-at-goal convention, and weight.

reference.title: EECBS: A Bounded-Suboptimal Search for Multi-Agent Path Finding

lacam_star.tagline: Choose a joint move only when the team can make it together.
lacam_star.story: A group of robots does not move through separate worlds. LaCAM* builds a joint configuration for the whole team, rejects conflicting combinations, and grows the search until all agents can reach their goals.
steps: Represent the team's positions together as one joint state.
Choose candidate moves and reject vertex or edge-swap conflicts.
Continue its seeded anytime search while agents respect reached goal locations.
lacam_star.experiment: Pause at a crowded crossing. A move can be legal for one robot and impossible for the group when all plans are considered together.
lacam_star.question: What happens after an agent reaches its goal in this project?
lacam_star.answer: It stays at that goal while the other agents continue, so the goal remains part of the joint collision constraints.
lacam_star.mechanism: LaCAM* searches whole-agent configurations at a high level, where one state contains every agent's location. A low-level constraint search lazily constructs the next joint configuration instead of enumerating every combination up front. The seeded anytime search keeps improving solutions; in this project, optimality is returned only when the open set is exhausted under the documented transition-cost objective.

example.setup: Two agents approach a one-cell doorway from opposite sides; moving either agent alone may create a conflict with the other's next step.
steps: A high-level node represents the locations of all agents at one time, along with the information needed to continue the search.
Low-level constraints generate a joint next move while avoiding occupied vertices and edge swaps.
A feasible joint configuration extends the plan; later search can improve its cost, and exhaustion of the open set is the condition for the project's optimal result.

lacam_star.best_for: Use it for undirected unit-weight MAPF with unique starts and goals, vertex and edge-swap conflicts, and agents staying at reached goals.
lacam_star.watch_out: The search's optimality condition depends on exhausting the open set and on cumulative transition costs matching the supported objective. A time-limited incumbent is not the same as an exhausted proof.
lacam_star.evaluation: Report conflict-free success, sum of transition costs, makespan, and time-to-first versus final solution. Use the same seeded instances and stop budgets, and distinguish exhausted runs from anytime incumbents.
metrics: Time to first and final solution

reference.title: Improving LaCAM for Scalable Eventually Optimal Multi-Agent Pathfinding
